shopify.title: Connect Shopify
shopify.description: OAuth connection. We never see your Shopify password.
steps: Enter your store domain below. This is the yourstore.myshopify.com URL you use to log into Shopify admin.
You'll be redirected to Shopify to authorize read-only access to your product catalog. We only request product scopes, never orders or customers.
After you approve, Shopify allows ecentic to read and write your store's product data.

woocommerce.title: Connect WooCommerce
woocommerce.description: One-click via the ecentic plugin, or manually with API keys.

oneClick.title: One-click connect
oneClick.description: Enter your store URL and approve the connection from your WordPress admin. There are no API keys to copy. You'll need the free écentic for WooCommerce plugin installed and activated first; if it isn't there yet, we'll show you how to add it. This also enables hosted UCP, which makes your store transactable by AI shopping agents.

installRequired.title: We couldn't find the écentic plugin on {store}.
steps: Install écentic for WooCommerce from your WordPress admin and activate it.
Either come back here and press Connect again, or open WooCommerce → UCP (AI Agents) in wp-admin and click Connect to ecentic.ai.

manual.title: Or connect manually: where to find your API keys
steps: Log into your WordPress admin panel and go to WooCommerce → Settings → Advanced → REST API.
Click Add key. Give it a description like "ecentic", set permissions to Read/Write if you want ecentic to push listing changes, or Read for sync-only, then click Generate.
Copy the Consumer key (starts with ck_) and Consumer secret (starts with cs_). You won't be able to see the secret again, so paste it here right away.

description.before: The public URL of your WooCommerce store, for example
description.after: . This is the homepage, not the WordPress admin URL.

consumerKey.label: Consumer Key
consumerKey.description: The key WooCommerce generated for you. It always starts with ck_ followed by a long alphanumeric string. We use this to authenticate API requests (catalog sync needs read access; publishing optimised listings from the dashboard needs read/write on the key).

consumerSecret.label: Consumer Secret
consumerSecret.description: The secret that pairs with the key, starting with cs_. WooCommerce shows it only once when you generate the key, so copy it before you leave.

googleShopping.label: Google Shopping XML
googleShopping.description: is the most common format. If you use Google Merchant Center, you already have one. It's an RSS/Atom feed where each <item> contains g:title, g:price, g:image_link, etc.

json.label: JSON
json.description: is a simple array of product objects. We look for title, price, image, and url fields. Nested under a products or items key is fine too.

description.before: The publicly accessible URL that serves your product feed. For example:
description.after: The URL must be reachable from the internet, so localhost and private-network URLs won't work. We auto-detect whether it's XML or JSON from the content.
